findings.title: User/installer verification is skipped whenever the Integration row does not already exist
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch the new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installer is reached only after `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` succeeds. When that lookup raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, and `build_integration` then creates the Integration. This is exactly the first-install path (it is also what happens whenever the GitHub `installation` webhook that populates `metadata["sender"]` has not been processed yet, since webhook delivery is not ordered relative to the browser redirect). Consequently the authenticated GitHub user is never compared to the installer on the primary flow; the check only runs on later re-install attempts. An attacker who starts an install with their own installation_id while the victim completes OAuth as a different GitHub account is not caught, which defeats the stated security fix. The verification needs to run (or fail closed) even when the Integration row is absent / the sender is not yet known.

findings.title: Unchecked metadata["sender"] access raises KeyError instead of showing the error page
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes `metadata` contains a `sender` dict with a `login` key. `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` only adds `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is set, and `test_basic_flow` asserts that pipeline-created integrations have metadata without `sender`. Any Integration whose metadata lacks `sender` (e.g. created by the pipeline itself, created by an older version, or whose metadata was overwritten by `build_integration`) will raise `KeyError` here, returning a 500 rather than the intended `github-integration-failed.html` error. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value as a verification failure.

findings.title: Token exchange and user-info fetch are not guarded, so upstream failures produce a 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is outside the try/except; the except only wraps `safe_urlread`. `safe_urlopen` raises on connection errors and non-2xx responses, and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) can raise `ApiError` as well. Those exceptions propagate and render a 500, not the friendly `github-integration-failed.html` page, contradicting the PR's claim that an invalid/reused code or failed token exchange always shows that error. Wrap the exchange and the user-info call in error handling and return `error(...)` on failure.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer covers the 404 installation-not-found path
findings.body: The test still stubs a 404 for `/app/installations/{id}`, but the requests it issues never reach `get_installation_info`/`build_integration`: the second GET uses a bogus `state` ("ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05") and the changed assertion now checks the generic "Invalid installation request." message emitted by OAuthLoginView's state-mismatch branch. The original assertion (`The GitHub installation could not be found.`) was removed, so the `ApiError` 404 → `IntegrationError` code path in `build_integration` is no longer tested by any test. Either keep a test that drives the pipeline to completion with a 404 or rename/repurpose this test and add coverage for the 404 branch.

findings.title: Runtime _() on error_short prevents these messages from being extracted for translation
findings.body: The refactor passes the user-facing strings as plain `error_short` arguments (`"GitHub installation pending deletion."`, `"Github installed on another Sentry organization."`, and the `"Invalid installation request."` default), then calls `_()` on the runtime variable inside `error()`. `gettext`/`makemessages` only extracts literals passed directly to `_()`, so these strings will no longer appear in the message catalog and will be shown untranslated (previously they were `_("...")` literals). Pass lazy literals at the call sites (or make the arguments default to `_()` literals) so they remain extractable.
